subject: Chemistry
examFormat: Three papers, all compulsory; Papers 1 and 2 form a composite paper taken at one sitting. Paper 1: 50 multiple-choice questions from Section A, 1 hour, 50 marks. Paper 2: 2-hour essay paper of 100 marks; Section A has ten short structured questions from the common portion (all answered, 25 marks); Section B has two questions from the common portion and two from the country-specific section (Section B or C), of which any three are answered at 25 marks each. Paper 3: 2-hour practical test for school candidates (1 hour 30 minutes alternative to practical for private candidates) with three compulsory questions for 50 marks: one on quantitative analysis, one on qualitative analysis and one on practical activities suggested in the teaching syllabus.
excluded: Section B (for candidates in Ghana only: mass spectrometer and nuclear chemistry, hybridization, Hess's law and Born-Haber cycle, pH/pOH and buffers, solubility product, rate law, equilibrium constants, additional organic chemistry, cement and mineral deposits in Ghana) was left out. In the practicals, the item marked for Ghanaians only (analysis of Na2CO3/NaHCO3 mixture by double indicator methods) was also left out.

subtopics.name: Measurement of physical quantities
objectives: Measure mass, length, time, temperature and volume
Use appropriate SI units and significant figures
Distinguish precision and accuracy in measurement
State the importance of scientific measurements in chemistry

subtopics.name: Scientific methods
objectives: Outline the scientific method: observation, hypothesis, experimentation, formulation of laws and theories

subtopics.name: Gross features of the atom
objectives: Give a short account of Dalton's atomic theory and its limitations, J.J. Thompson's experiment and Bohr's model of the atom
Outline Rutherford's alpha scattering experiment used to establish the structure of the atom

subtopics.name: Atomic number, isotopes and atomic mass
objectives: Explain the meaning and symbolic representation of atoms and sub-atomic particles
Define atomic number/proton number, number of neutrons, isotopes, atomic mass and mass number
Define relative atomic mass (Ar) and relative molecular mass (Mr) on the carbon-12 scale
Treat atomic mass as the weighted average mass of isotopes, using the calculation of relative atomic mass of chlorine as an example
Define the atomic mass unit

subtopics.name: Characteristics and nature of matter
objectives: Describe atoms, molecules and ions as particles and building blocks of matter

subtopics.name: Particulate nature of matter: physical and chemical changes
objectives: Explain physical and chemical changes with examples (physical: melting of solids, magnetization of iron, dissolution of salt; chemical: burning of wood, rusting of iron, decay of leaves)

subtopics.name: Electron configuration and orbitals
objectives: Write detailed electron configurations (s, p, d) for atoms of the first thirty elements
Explain the origin of s, p and d orbitals as sub-energy levels, and the shapes of s and p orbitals only
Apply the Aufbau principle, Hund's rule of maximum multiplicity and Pauli exclusion principle
Write abbreviated and detailed electron configurations in terms of s, p and d

topics.name: Standard Separation Techniques for Mixtures
objectives: Classify mixtures (solid-solid, solid-liquid, liquid-liquid, gas-gas) with examples
Describe separation techniques: crystallization, distillation, precipitation, magnetization, chromatography, sublimation etc.
Use boiling point for liquids and melting point for solids as criteria for purity

subtopics.name: Periodicity of the elements
objectives: Relate electron configurations to group and periodic classifications

subtopics.name: Categories of elements in the periodic table
objectives: Identify metals, semi-metals, non-metals, halogens, alkali metals, alkaline earth metals and transition metals in the periodic table

subtopics.name: Periodic law and trends
objectives: Explain the periodic law
Describe periodic properties: atomic size, ionic size, ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity
Account for simple discrepancies in respect to beryllium, boron, oxygen and nitrogen
Describe the periodic gradation of the elements in the third period (Na - Ar): progression from metallic to non-metallic character and from ionic to covalent bonding in compounds
State differences and similarities in properties between second and third period elements

subtopics.name: Reactions of acids with metals, oxides and trioxocarbonates (IV)
objectives: Describe the reactions of acids with period three metals (Na, Mg, Al) and period four metals (K, Ca), their oxides and trioxocarbonates (IV)
Write chemical equations and state the pH of solutions of the metallic oxides and trioxocarbonates

subtopics.name: Periodic gradation of the halogens
objectives: Recognize group variations in group seven (F, Cl, Br, I), noting any anomalies

Treat physical states, melting and boiling points, variable oxidation states, redox properties, displacement of one halogen by another, and reaction of the elements with water and alkali (balanced equations required)

subtopics.name: Elements of the first transition series
objectives: Describe the electron configurations, physical properties (physical states, metallic and magnetic properties) and chemical reactivity of the elements 21Sc - 30Zn and their compounds
Compare the reactivity of the metals with air, water and acids with s-block elements (Li, Na, Be, Mg)
State other properties of transition metals: variable oxidation states, coloured compounds, complex formation, catalytic abilities, paramagnetism and hardness

subtopics.name: Interatomic bonding
objectives: Explain the meaning of chemical bonding
Write Lewis dot structures for simple ionic and covalent compounds

subtopics.name: Ionic bonds and compounds
objectives: Describe the formation of stable compounds from ions, and the factors influencing formation: ionization energy, electron affinity and electronegativity difference
State the properties of ionic compounds: solubility in polar and non-polar solvents, electrical conductivity, hardness and melting point
Name simple ionic compounds using the IUPAC system

subtopics.name: Covalent bonds and compounds
objectives: Describe the formation of covalent bonds and the factors influencing it: electron affinity, ionization energy, atomic size and electronegativity
State the properties of covalent compounds: solubility in polar and non-polar solvents, melting point, boiling point and electrical conductivity
Distinguish pure covalent from coordinate (dative) covalent bonds

subtopics.name: Shapes of molecular compounds
objectives: Describe linear, planar and tetrahedral shapes for compounds such as BeCl2, BF3, CH4, NH3 and CO2

subtopics.name: Metallic bonding
objectives: Describe metallic bonding and the factors influencing its formation: atomic radius, ionization energy and number of valence electrons
State the typical properties of metals: heat and electrical conductivity, malleability, lustre, ductility, sonority and hardness

subtopics.name: Intermolecular bonding
objectives: Compare the relative physical properties of polar and non-polar compounds
Describe the formation and nature of hydrogen bonding
Treat dipole-dipole, induced dipole-dipole and induced dipole-induced dipole forces under van der Waals forces
Explain variation in melting and boiling points of noble gases, halogens and alkanes using van der Waals forces, and boiling points of H2O and H2S using hydrogen bonding
Compare all bond types

subtopics.name: Symbols, formulae and equations
objectives: Write symbols of the first thirty elements and other common elements
Determine empirical and molecular formulae
Calculate percentage composition of an element and mass and volume relationships in reactions
Write chemical equations and IUPAC names for combustion (including simple hydrocarbons), synthesis, displacement or replacement, decomposition and ionic reactions
State the laws of conservation of mass, constant composition and multiple proportions, and use them to balance equations
Illustrate the law of conservation of mass experimentally

subtopics.name: Amount of substance
objectives: Make mass and volume measurements
Use the mole as a unit of measurement and Avogadro's constant, L = 6.02 x 10^23 entities per mol
Use molar quantities and moles of electrons, atoms, molecules and formula units

subtopics.name: Mole ratios
objectives: Use mole ratios to determine the stoichiometry of chemical reactions
Calculate number of entities, amount of substance, mass, concentration, volume and percentage yield of product

subtopics.name: Solutions and concentration terms
objectives: Describe a solution as made up of solvent and solute
Distinguish dilute from concentrated solutions and basic, acidic and neutral solutions
Express concentration as mass concentration (g dm^-3) and molar concentration (mol dm^-3), using current IUPAC terminology

subtopics.name: Standard solutions
objectives: Prepare primary standards, e.g. anhydrous Na2CO3 and (COOH)2.2H2O
Explain the terms primary standard, secondary standard and standard solution

subtopics.name: Preparation of solutions by dilution
objectives: Prepare solutions from liquid solutes by dilution using the dilution factor

subtopics.name: Kinetic theory of matter
objectives: State the postulates of the kinetic theory of matter
Use the theory to explain melting of solids, boiling and evaporation of liquids, dissolution of solutes, Brownian motion and diffusion

subtopics.name: Changes of state of matter
objectives: Explain changes of state in terms of movement of particles, noting that randomness decreases from gas to liquid to solid and vice versa
Illustrate changes of state using different forms of water, iodine, sulphur, naphthalene etc.
Illustrate Brownian motion by experiment (pollen grains/powdered sulphur in water, smoke in a glass container, or a dusty room swept and viewed in sunlight)

subtopics.name: Diffusion
objectives: Demonstrate diffusion of two gases experimentally
Relate the speed of gas particles to the masses of particles
Demonstrate diffusion of solute particles in liquids

subtopics.name: Gases
objectives: Describe the characteristics and nature of gases: arrangement of particles, density, shape and compressibility
State and explain the gas laws (Charles', Boyle's, Dalton's law of partial pressure, Graham's law of diffusion, Avogadro's law) and the ideal gas equation PV = nRT using the kinetic model
Distinguish ideal and real gases and the factors responsible for deviation of real gases
Prepare, purify and collect H2, NH3 and CO2 in the laboratory and state their physical and chemical properties

subtopics.name: Liquids
objectives: Describe the characteristics and nature of liquids based on arrangement of particles, shape, volume, compressibility, density and viscosity

subtopics.name: Vapour and gases
objectives: Explain vapour, vapour pressure, saturated vapour pressure, boiling and evaporation
Distinguish between vapour and gas
Explain the effect of vapour pressure on boiling points and boiling at reduced pressure

subtopics.name: Solids
objectives: Describe the characteristics, nature, types and structures of solids: ionic, metallic, covalent network and molecular, with examples
Describe arrangements of particles (ions, molecules and atoms) in the solid state
Relate the properties of solids to the type of interatomic and intermolecular bonding, including the bonds in graphite

subtopics.name: Diamond and graphite
objectives: Describe the structures, properties and uses of diamond and graphite
State the use of iodine in everyday life

subtopics.name: Melting points of covalent solids
objectives: Determine melting points of covalent solids as an indicator of purity, e.g. benzoic acid, oxalic acid and ethanamide

subtopics.name: Energy and enthalpy
objectives: Explain the terms energy and enthalpy
Describe energy changes associated with chemical processes

subtopics.name: Energy changes and their effects
objectives: Distinguish exothermic and endothermic processes
Describe the total energy of a system as the sum of various forms of energy e.g. kinetic, potential, electrical, heat and sound
Describe enthalpy changes in combustion, dissolution and neutralization

subtopics.name: Definitions of acids and bases
objectives: Define acids and bases using Arrhenius concepts in terms of H3O+ and OH- ions in water
Describe the effects of acids and bases on indicators, Zn, Fe and trioxocarbonate (IV) and hydrogentrioxocarbonate (IV) salts

subtopics.name: Properties of acids and bases
objectives: Describe characteristic properties in aqueous solution: conductivities, taste, litmus/indicators and feel
Write balanced chemical equations of all reactions

subtopics.name: Acids, bases and salts as electrolytes
objectives: Distinguish electrolytes and non-electrolytes and strong and weak electrolytes
Use conductivity and enthalpy of neutralization as evidence

subtopics.name: Classification of acids and bases
objectives: Classify acids and bases into strong and weak using the extent of dissociation in water and conductivity
Describe the behaviour of weak acids and weak bases in water as examples of equilibrium systems

subtopics.name: Concept of pH
objectives: Define pH and describe the pH scale
Measure pH of solutions using a pH meter, colorimetric methods or universal indicator
State the significance of pH in everyday life e.g. acid rain, pH of soil, blood and urine

subtopics.name: Salts
objectives: Define salts and describe types: normal, acidic, basic, double and complex salts
Describe laboratory and industrial preparation of salts, including mining of impure sodium chloride and conversion into granulated salt, and preparation of NaOH, Cl2 and H2
State the uses of salts

subtopics.name: Hydrolysis of salts
objectives: Explain how salts form acidic, alkaline and neutral aqueous solutions
Describe the behaviour of NH4Cl, AlCl3, Na2CO3 and CH3COONa in water as equilibrium systems
Explain the effects of charge density of cations and anions on hydrolysis, with examples from group 1, 2, 3 and the d-block

subtopics.name: Deliquescent, efflorescent and hygroscopic compounds
objectives: Distinguish deliquescent, efflorescent and hygroscopic compounds and emphasize the use of hygroscopic compounds as drying agents

subtopics.name: Acid-base indicators
objectives: Describe qualitatively how an acid-base indicator works
Explain indicators as weak organic acids or bases (organic dyes), colour dependence on pH and the working pH ranges of methyl orange and phenolphthalein

subtopics.name: Acid-base titration
objectives: Use relevant apparatus correctly and explain how indicators work in titrations
Carry out titrations involving HCl, HNO3, H2SO4 and NaOH, KOH, Ca(OH)2, CO3^2- and HCO3-
Carry out titrations of weak acid versus strong base, strong acid versus weak base and strong acid versus strong base using appropriate indicators
Apply titration to quantitative determination of concentration, mole ratio, purity, water of crystallization and composition

subtopics.name: General principles of solubility
objectives: Explain the meaning of solubility, and saturated and unsaturated solutions
Describe a saturated solution as an equilibrium system
Express solubility in mol dm^-3 and g dm^-3 of solution/solvent
Use solubility curves and describe the effect of temperature on solubility
Relate solubility to crystallization and describe crystallization/recrystallization as a method of purification
Identify soluble and insoluble salts of stated cations and anions
Carry out calculations on solubility

subtopics.name: Practical application of solubility
objectives: Explain solubility rules and apply generalizations about solubility of salts to qualitative analysis of Pb2+, Ca2+, Al3+, Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+, Zn2+, NH4+, Cl-, Br-, I-, SO4^2-, S^2-, CO3^2- and SO3^2-

subtopics.name: Rate of reactions
objectives: Define reaction rate and identify observable physical changes: colour, mass, temperature, pH and formation of precipitate

subtopics.name: Factors affecting rates
objectives: Explain the effect of physical states, concentration/pressure of reactants, temperature, catalysts, light, particle size and nature of reactants, with an experimental demonstration for each

subtopics.name: Theories of reaction rates
objectives: Treat collision and transition state theories qualitatively
Explain factors influencing collisions (temperature and concentration), effective collision and activation energy
Draw an energy profile showing activation energy and enthalpy change

subtopics.name: Analysis and interpretation of graphs
objectives: Draw and interpret graphs and charts of reaction rates

subtopics.name: Equilibrium: general principles
objectives: Explain reversible and irreversible reactions and dynamic equilibrium
Treat the equilibrium constant K qualitatively, stressing that K is constant at constant temperature
Demonstrate reversible reactions by a simple experiment

subtopics.name: Le Chatelier's principle
objectives: Predict the effects of changes in concentration, temperature, pressure and volume on equilibrium systems

subtopics.name: Oxidation and reduction process
objectives: Describe oxidation and reduction in terms of addition/removal of oxygen and hydrogen, loss and gain of electrons, and change in oxidation numbers/states
Determine oxidation numbers/states

subtopics.name: Oxidizing and reducing agents
objectives: Describe oxidizing and reducing agents in terms of oxygen and hydrogen, electrons and oxidation numbers/states

subtopics.name: Redox equations
objectives: Balance redox equations by ion, electron or change in oxidation number/state methods, and by half reactions and overall reaction

subtopics.name: Electrochemical cells
objectives: Explain the standard hydrogen electrode and the meaning and measurement of standard electrode potential (E0), using metal/metal ion systems only
Draw cell diagrams and write cell notation
Describe electrochemical cells as a combination of two half-cells and the meaning of magnitude and sign of e.m.f.
Distinguish primary and secondary cells and describe the Daniell cell, lead acid battery, dry cells and fuel cells as generators of electrical energy

subtopics.name: Electrolysis
objectives: Define electrolysis and compare electrolytic and electrochemical cells
Explain the mechanism of electrolysis and the factors influencing the discharge of species
Limit electrolytes to molten PbBr2 and NaCl, dilute and concentrated NaCl solution, CuSO4(aq), dilute H2SO4, NaOH(aq) and CaCl2(aq), using platinum or graphite and copper electrodes
State and apply Faraday's laws using 1 F = 96,500 C and mole ratios
Describe practical applications: electroplating, and extraction and purification of metals

subtopics.name: Corrosion of metals
objectives: Treat corrosion as a redox process and describe rusting of iron and its economic costs
Describe prevention based on electrode potentials (galvanizing, sacrificial/cathodic protection) and non-redox methods (painting, greasing/oiling)

topics.name: Chemistry of Carbon Compounds
topics.content: Examples of isomerism should be limited to compounds having a maximum of five carbon atoms. Alkanes include uses of haloalkanes and pollution effects.

subtopics.name: Classification of carbon compounds
objectives: Classify organic compounds broadly into straight chain, branched chain, aromatic and alicyclic compounds

subtopics.name: Functional groups
objectives: Name systematically compounds with the functional groups: alkanes, alkenes, alkynes, hydroxyl compounds (aliphatic and aromatic), alkanoic acids, alkyl alkanoates (esters and salts) and amines

subtopics.name: Separation and purification of organic compounds
objectives: Discuss distillation, crystallization, drying and chromatography

subtopics.name: Petroleum/crude oil
objectives: Describe composition and classification of petroleum
Describe fractional distillation and major products
Describe cracking and reforming
State sources and uses of petrochemicals as starting materials of organic synthesis
Explain quality of petrol and the meaning and importance of octane number

subtopics.name: Determination of formulae and structures of organic compounds
objectives: Determine empirical and molecular formulae and molecular structures of organic compounds

subtopics.name: General properties of organic compounds
objectives: Describe a homologous series: gradation in physical properties and effects of introducing active groups into the inert alkane
Distinguish structural from geometric/stereo isomerism

subtopics.name: Alkanes
objectives: Describe laboratory and industrial preparations and other sources of alkanes
Describe nomenclature and structure
Describe reactivity: combustion, substitution reactions and cracking of large alkane molecules
State uses as fuels and as starting materials for synthesis, and uses of haloalkanes and pollution effects

subtopics.name: Alkenes
objectives: Describe laboratory preparation, nomenclature and structure of alkenes
Describe addition reactions with halogens, hydrogen, bromine water, hydrogen halides and acidified water
Describe oxidation (hydroxylation with aqueous KMnO4) and polymerization
State uses of alkenes
Use reaction with Br2/water, Br2/CCl4 and KMnO4(aq) as laboratory detection of alkenes

subtopics.name: Alkynes
objectives: Describe nomenclature and structure of alkynes, and industrial production and uses of ethyne
Distinguish terminal from non-terminal alkynes and alkane, alkene and alkyne by tests
Describe chemical reactions: halogenation, combustion, hydration and hydrogenation

subtopics.name: Benzene
objectives: Describe the structure and physical properties of benzene, including resonance and stability leading to substitution reactions
Describe chemical properties: addition reactions (hydrogenation and halogenation, mechanism not required) and compare with those of alkenes

subtopics.name: Alkanols
objectives: Describe sources, nomenclature and structure of alkanols, including laboratory preparation (hydration of alkenes) and industrial and local production of ethanol and alcoholic beverages
Mention harmful impurities and methods of purification
Recognize the structure of mono-, di- and triols and classify alkanols as primary, secondary and tertiary
State physical properties: boiling point and solubility in water, including hydrogen bonding effect
Describe reactions with Na, alkanoic acids (esterification) and conc. H2SO4, and oxidation by KMnO4(aq), K2Cr2O7(aq) and I2 in NaOH(aq)
State the laboratory test for ethanol and the uses of alkanols

subtopics.name: Alkanoic acids
objectives: Describe sources, nomenclature and structure (methanoic acid - insect bite; ethanoic acid - vinegar) and recognize mono and dioic acids
State physical properties: boiling point and solubility in water, including hydrogen bonding effect
Describe acid properties only: reactions with H2O, NaOH, NH3, NaHCO3, Zn and Mg
State the laboratory test (reaction with NaHCO3, Na2CO3) and uses of ethanoic and benzoic acids

subtopics.name: Alkanoates as derivatives of alkanoic acids
objectives: Describe sources, nomenclature, preparation and structure of alkyl alkanoates (esters) from alkanoic acids
State physical properties: solubility, boiling and melting point
Describe hydrolysis of alkyl alkanoates (mechanism not required)
State uses: soap production, flavouring agent, plasticizers, solvents and perfumes

subtopics.name: Chemical industry
objectives: Identify natural resources in the candidate's own country
Identify chemical industries in the candidate's own country and their raw materials
Distinguish fine from heavy chemicals
State factors that determine location of chemical industries and the effect of industries on the community

subtopics.name: Pollution
objectives: Describe air, water and soil pollution: sources, effects and control
Explain the greenhouse effect and depletion of the ozone layer
Distinguish biodegradable and non-biodegradable pollutants

subtopics.name: Biotechnology
objectives: Describe food processing and fermentation, including production of gari, bread and alcoholic beverages e.g. local gin

subtopics.name: Proteins
objectives: Describe proteins as polymers of amino acid molecules linked by peptide or amide linkage
Describe sources and properties, e.g. solubility, hydrolysis of proteins, and laboratory tests using Ninhydrin, Biuret or Millon's reagent
State the uses of protein

subtopics.name: Amino acids
objectives: Describe the nomenclature and general structure of amino acids and their difunctional nature

subtopics.name: Fats and oils
objectives: Describe sources (animals and plants) and properties: solubility, acidic and alkaline hydrolysis, hydrogenation and test for fats and oil
Describe the general structure of fats/oils as mono-, di- and tri- esters of propane-1,2,3-triol (glycerol)
Describe preparation of soap (saponification) and compare soap and detergents and their action on soft and hard water
State uses of fats/oils

subtopics.name: Carbohydrates
objectives: Classify carbohydrates as monosaccharides, disaccharides and polysaccharides, with names and components
Describe properties: solubility of sugars, hydrolysis of disaccharides into monosaccharides, and tests for reducing sugars using sugar strips, Fehling's, Benedict's or Tollen's reagent
Describe starch as a polymer made up of glucose units and condensation of monosaccharides to form disaccharides and polysaccharides
State uses of carbohydrates

subtopics.name: Synthetic polymers
objectives: Define monomers, polymers and polymerization
Distinguish addition and condensation polymerization and classify and prepare polymers based on monomers and comonomers
Describe properties: thermoplastics and thermosets, and modification of properties of polymers
State uses of polymers, including plastics and resins
Carry out chemical tests on plastics using heat, acids and alkalis

topics.name: Non-metals and their Compounds
topics.content: Tests for oxygen, hydrogen and water are required. Uses of halogen compounds include silver halide in photography and sodium oxochlorate (I) as a bleaching agent. Both laboratory and industrial preparations of oxygen (from liquefied air) are required. For trioxonitrate (V) salts, action of heat and test for trioxonitrate (V) ions are required. The contact process should be discussed.

subtopics.name: Carbon
objectives: Describe the allotropes of carbon (graphite, diamond and amorphous carbon): structures, properties and uses correlated with structure, and combustion of allotropes
Describe types of coal (anthracite, peat, lignite), destructive distillation of coal and uses of the products
Describe classification and uses of coke, and manufacture of synthetic gas (water gas and producer gas) and uses
Describe laboratory preparation, properties, uses and test of carbon (IV) oxide; properties and uses of carbon (II) oxide
Describe trioxocarbonate (IV) salts: solubility, action of heat, reaction with dilute acid, and uses

subtopics.name: Oxygen
objectives: Describe laboratory and industrial preparation of oxygen
Describe properties and uses of oxygen
Describe binary compounds of oxygen: acidic, basic, amphoteric and neutral oxides

subtopics.name: Hydrogen
objectives: Describe laboratory preparations of hydrogen
Describe properties and uses of hydrogen

subtopics.name: Water and solution
objectives: Describe the composition of water, with reference to electrolysis of acidified water, and the test for water
Describe water as a solvent
Describe hardness of water, its causes and methods of removing it, with advantages and disadvantages of hard and soft water and experiments comparing degrees of hardness
Describe treatment of water for town supply

subtopics.name: Halogens
objectives: Describe the laboratory preparation, properties and reactions of chlorine, including redox properties and displacement of one halogen by another
Describe variable oxidation states and reaction of halogens with water and alkali (balanced equation required)
Describe laboratory preparation, properties and uses of hydrogen chloride gas, with the test for HCl gas and fountain experiment
State uses of halogen compounds

subtopics.name: Nitrogen
objectives: Describe preparation, properties and uses of nitrogen from liquefied air
Describe laboratory and industrial preparation, properties, uses and test of ammonia, including fountain experiment
Describe laboratory preparation, properties and uses of trioxonitrate (V) acid
Describe trioxonitrate (V) salts: action of heat and test for trioxonitrate (V) ions

subtopics.name: Sulphur
objectives: Describe allotropes and uses of sulphur
Describe compounds of sulphur, including trioxosulphate (IV) acids and its salts
Describe industrial preparation (contact process), reactions and uses of tetraoxosulphate (VI) acid

subtopics.name: The noble gases
objectives: Describe the properties and uses of the noble gases

topics.name: Metals and their Compounds
topics.content: Compounds of sodium must be limited to NaCl, NaOH, Na2CO3, NaNO3, Na2SO4 and NaClO. Compounds of calcium must be limited to CaCO3, CaO, CaSO4, CaCl2 and Ca(OH)2. Compounds of copper must be limited to CuSO4, CuO and CuCl2.

subtopics.name: Extraction of metals
objectives: Describe the extraction of aluminium, iron and tin, covering raw materials, processing, main products and by-products
State the uses of the metals

subtopics.name: Alloys
objectives: Describe common alloys of Cu, Al, Pb, Fe and Sn and their uses

subtopics.name: Sodium and its compounds
objectives: Describe the properties and uses of sodium and its compounds

subtopics.name: Calcium and its compounds
objectives: Describe the properties and uses of calcium and its compounds

subtopics.name: Reactivity of iron and aluminium
objectives: Describe the reactivity of iron and aluminium with air, water and acids

subtopics.name: Copper and its compounds
objectives: Describe the properties and uses of copper and its compounds

topics.name: Practical Chemistry
topics.content: General skills and principles: measurement of mass and volume; preparation and dilution of standard solutions; filtration, recrystallisation and melting point determination; measurement of heats of neutralization and solution; determination of pH of various solutions by colorimetry; determination of rates of reaction from concentration versus time curves; determination of equilibrium constants for simple systems. Quantitative analysis: acid-base titrations using standard solutions of acids and alkalis and the indicators methyl orange, methyl red and phenolphthalein to determine concentrations of acid and alkaline solutions, molar masses of acids and bases and water of crystallization, solubility, percentage purity of acids and bases and stoichiometry of reactions; redox titrations of acidic MnO4- with Fe2+, acidic MnO4- with C2O4^2-, and I2 in KI versus S2O3^2-. Qualitative analysis (no formal scheme of analysis required): characteristic tests of the cations NH4+, Ca2+, Pb2+, Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+, Al3+ and Zn2+ with dilute NaOH(aq) and NH3(aq) and confirmatory tests; characteristic reactions of dilute HCl on solids or aqueous solutions and conc. H2SO4 on solid samples of Cl-, SO3^2-, CO3^2-, NO3- and SO4^2- and confirmatory tests for these anions; comparative study of the halogens and displacement reactions; characteristic tests for the gases H2, NH3, CO2, HCl and SO2; characteristic test tube reactions of functional groups in alkenes, alkanols, alkanoic acids, sugars (Fehling's and Benedict's solutions only), starch (iodine test only) and proteins (Ninhydrin, Xanthoproteic, Biuret and Millon's tests only).

subtopics.name: General practical skills and principles
objectives: Measure mass and volume
Prepare and dilute standard solutions
Carry out filtration, recrystallisation and melting point determination
Measure heats of neutralization and solution
Determine pH of various solutions by colorimetry
Determine rates of reaction from concentration versus time curves
Determine equilibrium constants for simple systems

subtopics.name: Quantitative analysis
objectives: Carry out acid-base titrations to determine concentrations, molar masses, water of crystallization, solubility, percentage purity and stoichiometry
Carry out redox titrations of acidic MnO4- with Fe2+ and with C2O4^2-, and I2 in KI versus S2O3^2-

subtopics.name: Qualitative analysis
objectives: Carry out characteristic and confirmatory tests of the cations NH4+, Ca2+, Pb2+, Cu2+, Fe2+, Fe3+, Al3+ and Zn2+ with dilute NaOH(aq) and NH3(aq)
Carry out characteristic and confirmatory tests of the anions Cl-, SO3^2-, CO3^2-, NO3- and SO4^2-
Carry out a comparative study of the halogens and displacement reactions
Test for the gases H2, NH3, CO2, HCl and SO2
Carry out test tube reactions of functional groups in alkenes, alkanols, alkanoic acids, sugars, starch and proteins
